messages.author: f8335ec6134e45e8
messages.subject: Using splines in RStan
parts:
Hi there,
I am trying to create STAN code for a model using spline terms which I have created outside of the stan code:

week.index <- dat$week.index

smooth.week.index <- s(week.index, bs="cr", k=30)

dat$spline_WeekIndex <- smooth.construct(smooth.week.index, dat, knots=NULL)$X


I then create my matrix of predictors:


X <- cbind(Intercept=1, dat$spline_WeekIndex, other predictors..)


and this is my model:


N <- dim(X)[1]

k <- dim(X)[2]

Outcome <- dat$Outcome


data <- list(N=N, X=X, k=k, Outcome=Outcome)


stan_code<-"

data {

    

    int<lower=0> N; 

    int<lower=0> k; //no. of predictors

    real Outcome[N]; //outcome

    matrix[N, k] X; //predictor matrix

     }


parameters {

vector[k] alpha;

real <lower=0> taud;

}

model {

    vector[N] mu;

    

    mu <- X*alpha;


    alpha ~ normal(0,1000);

    taud ~ uniform(0,1000);

DeathRate ~ normal(mu, tau);



}"


I am having real trouble getting this to converge and when it finally does (after many iterations and a long wait to get the Rhat values close to 1) the neff values for the spline terms are all the same and very small which I think means it hasn’t mixed correctly?


Any suggestions how I could make this mix better and run faster?


Thanks in advance

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using splines in RStan
parts:
Hi, I don’t understand your model as it includes a variable, DeathRate, that doesn’t seem to be defined in your Stan code.  But, in any case, I don’t think normal(0,1000) priors are a good idea.  Better to use something informative.  And uniform(0,1000) is an even worse idea.  Better to use soft constraints than hard constraints.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using splines in RStan
parts:
Thanks for the reply.
I have tried rescaling some of my data so that the coefficients are all of magnitude 1 and have tried some more informative priors for alpha and tau but I am still finding it struggles to converge and the neff values are very small (<10) even when using 100000 iterations.
Any other clues as to what could be the problem? This is my code now (I have also rewritten the spline terms inside the stan code):

X <- cbind(Intercept=1, dat$h1n1_rate_ILI, dat$h3n2_rate_ILI, dat$ph1n1_rate_ILI, dat$ph1n1_rate_ILI_Pandemic, dat$B_rate_ILI, dat$RSV_rate_ILI, dat$TEMP, dat$TEMP2, dat$TEMP3, dat$AH, dat$AH2, dat$AH3, dat$NameChange)

N <- dim(X)[1]

k <- dim(X)[2]

DeathRate <- dat$DeathRate

WeekIndex <- dat$week.index

H <- 30 #no. of knots

xi <- seq(1,761, 761/30)


data <- list(N=N, X=X, k=k, DeathRate=DeathRate, WeekIndex=WeekIndex, H=H, xi=xi)


stan_code<-"

data {

    

    int<lower=0> N; //no. of weeks
int<lower=0> k; //no. of predictors
real DeathRate[N]; //outcome
matrix[N, k] X; //predictor matrix

vector[N] WeekIndex; // vector for spline function

    

    int<lower=0> H;

    vector[H] xi;

    }


transformed data {

    matrix[N, H+4] week_s;

    matrix[N, k+H+4] Z;

    for(n in 1:N) {

        week_s[n,1] <- WeekIndex[n]^0;

        week_s[n,2] <- WeekIndex[n]^1;

        week_s[n,3] <- WeekIndex[n]^2;

        week_s[n,4] <- WeekIndex[n]^3;

        for(h in 1:H)

        week_s[n,h+4] <- fmax(0,(WeekIndex[n] - xi[h])^3);

    }

    Z <- append_col(X, week_s);

  }


parameters {

vector[k+H+4] alpha;

real <lower=0> taud;

}

model {

    vector[N] mud;

    

    mud <- Z*alpha;


    alpha ~ normal(0,10);

  taud ~ cauchy(0,5);

DeathRate ~ normal(mud, taud);



}"


Thanks in advance!
